title: 43. Numeracy & Number Systems: Comparing Fractions and Decimals
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Comparing a Fraction and a Decimal
questions.learningObjective: Compare a common fraction with a decimal by converting them to a common form.
questions.question: Which comparison is correct?
questions.explanation: Convert \(\frac{3}{4}\) to a decimal: \(3 \div 4 = 0.75\). Since \(0.75 > 0.72\), we have \(\frac{3}{4} > 0.72\).
questions.hint: Convert the fraction to a decimal, then compare the digits by place value.

questions.concept: Comparing a Fraction and a Decimal
questions.learningObjective: Compare a fraction with a decimal using an equivalent decimal representation.
questions.question: Which comparison is correct?
questions.hint: Write both numbers with the same decimal place value before comparing them.

questions.concept: Comparing Fractions and Decimals by Conversion
questions.learningObjective: Convert a fraction to a decimal and compare values to the thousandths place.
questions.question: Compare \(\frac{5}{8}\) and \(0.62\). Which statement is correct?
questions.hint: Convert the fraction to a decimal and compare the values to the same number of decimal places.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize when a fraction and a decimal represent the same value.
questions.question: Which statement correctly compares \(0.45\) and \(\frac{9}{20}\)?
questions.explanation: Convert \(\frac{9}{20}\) to hundredths: \(\frac{9}{20}=\frac{45}{100}=0.45\). Therefore, \(0.45\) and \(\frac{9}{20}\) are equal.
questions.hint: Express the fraction with a denominator of \(100\), then compare the two values.

questions.concept: Selecting the Greater Fraction or Decimal
questions.learningObjective: Determine which of a fraction and a decimal has the greater value.
questions.question: Which number is greater?
questions.explanation: Convert \(\frac{7}{8}\) to a decimal: \(\frac{7}{8}=0.875\). Write \(0.8\) as \(0.800\). Since \(0.875 > 0.800\), \(\frac{7}{8}\) is greater.
questions.hint: Convert the fraction to a decimal, then compare corresponding place values.

questions.concept: Comparing Close Fraction and Decimal Values
questions.learningObjective: Compare close fraction and decimal values accurately using equivalent representations.
questions.question: Which comparison is correct?
questions.hint: Write both values to the thousandths place before deciding which is greater.

questions.concept: Identifying the Smaller Fraction or Decimal
questions.learningObjective: Identify the smaller value when comparing a fraction with a nearby decimal.
questions.question: Which number is smaller?
questions.explanation: Convert \(\frac{7}{10}\) to a decimal: \(\frac{7}{10}=0.70\). Since \(0.70 < 0.71\), \(\frac{7}{10}\) is smaller.
questions.hint: Express the fraction as a decimal with hundredths, then compare.

questions.concept: Comparing Fractions and Decimals in Measurement
questions.learningObjective: Compare a fractional measurement with a decimal measurement.
questions.question: Ribbon P is \(0.58\text{ m}\) long. Ribbon Q is \(\frac{3}{5}\text{ m}\) long. Which ribbon is longer?
questions.explanation: Convert \(\frac{3}{5}\) to a decimal: \(\frac{3}{5}=0.6=0.60\). Since \(0.60 > 0.58\), Ribbon Q is longer.
questions.hint: Convert the fractional length to a decimal, then compare the two lengths.

questions.concept: Comparing a Non-Terminating Fraction Decimal with a Finite Decimal
questions.learningObjective: Compare a fraction whose decimal form continues with a nearby finite decimal.
questions.question: Which comparison is correct?
questions.explanation: Compute \(17 \div 24\). This gives \(0.70833\ldots\). Compare it with \(0.71000\ldots\). Since \(0.70833\ldots < 0.71000\ldots\), \(\frac{17}{24} < 0.71\).
questions.hint: Convert the fraction to enough decimal places to determine its position relative to \(0.71\).

questions.concept: Comparing Distance from a Benchmark Decimal
questions.learningObjective: Compare a fraction and a decimal by determining which value is closer to a given benchmark.
questions.question: Which number is closer to \(0.81\)?
questions.explanation: Convert \(\frac{13}{16}\) to a decimal: \(\frac{13}{16}=0.8125\). Its distance from \(0.81\) is \(0.0025\). The distance from \(0.805\) to \(0.81\) is \(0.005\). Since \(0.0025 < 0.005\), \(\frac{13}{16}\) is closer to \(0.81\).
questions.hint: Convert the fraction to a decimal, then compare how far each value is from the benchmark.
